paper.title: What Memory Do GUI Agents Really Need? From Passive Records to Active Task-Driving States
paper.central_claim: GUI-agent memory should be an actively maintained task-driving execution state (ATMem: workflow phase, constraints, schema and per-item remaining/finished/skipped status, updated by the agent each step) rather than passive records; trained with SFT on verifier-gated rollouts and STR-GRPO (memory-on/off interventional online RL with a memory-cost reward), this yields ATMem-UI-8B at 76.6% on AndroidWorld (+3.3 over UI-TARS-2-230B, +5.9 over MAI-UI-8B), 23.3% on MobileWorld (unseen environments), and the best end-to-end results on the new DataScope benchmark.
paper.claim_scope: Mobile Android agents (Qwen3-VL-4B/8B); long-horizon, data-dependent workflows; AndroidWorld, MobileWorld and an author-built 96-instance benchmark (DataScope).

evidence.quote: we propose Active Task Driving Memory (ATMem), which shifts GUI-agent memory from passive storage to an actively maintained execution state.
evidence.support_explanation: Central proposal.

evidence.quote: With an 8B model, ATMem-UI achieves 76.6% success rate on AndroidWorld, outperforming UI-TARS-2-230B by 3.3 percentage points and the same-sized MAI-UI by 5.9 points.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline SOTA claim.

evidence.quote: Existing methods treat memory largely as passive storage, where past observations are accumulated and retrieved when needed.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap.

evidence.quote: Yet retrieving a value does not reveal its current role in the workflow.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism of the stated failure: roles/status of retrieved values are not represented.

evidence.quote: AndroidWorld statistics show that 83% of tasks involve data operations.
evidence.support_explanation: Scope claim for how general the problem is (statistic derived by authors).

evidence.quote: Schema.ItemContent enumerates instantiated data units, each indexed by a stable identifier
evidence.support_explanation: ATMem item entries carry identifiers, structured fields and a remaining/finished/skipped status.

evidence.quote: is inserted into the system prompt as the current task-driving memory
evidence.support_explanation: ATMem is a prompt-carried state that the model itself updates every step.

evidence.quote: A trajectory is retained only if its terminal environment state passes the corresponding task verifier.
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier-gated selection of SFT trajectories.

evidence.quote: This verifier-gated process yields 21,713 step-level SFT samples.
evidence.support_explanation: SFT dataset size.

evidence.quote: We construct 120 task templates, each human-designed and verified
evidence.support_explanation: Training task space is built from 120 human-designed templates.

evidence.quote: we run an online rollout framework that combines an LLM planner ( OpenAI, 2025 ) with UIIns ( Chen et al., 2025 )
evidence.support_explanation: SFT rollouts come from a GPT-5-class planner with a grounding model: a distillation teacher.

evidence.quote: We use a virtual Android platform containing 20 applications for both SFT trajectory collection and online RL training.
evidence.support_explanation: Training environment has 20 apps; AndroidWorld also has 20 apps (E024) and its construction practice is followed (App A.6), but overlap with evaluation tasks is not stated.

evidence.quote: During paired rollouts, we intervene on the explicit ATMem channel by enabling or masking memory access while keeping the task initialization unchanged.
evidence.support_explanation: STR-GRPO core operation: balanced memory-ON/OFF rollouts.

evidence.quote: restricts the memory cost to memory-ON rollouts, where ATMem is propagated across turns
evidence.support_explanation: Memory-cost penalty applies only to ON rollouts.

evidence.quote: For memory-OFF rollouts, ATMem block tokens are masked from the loss, and the loss covers only the reasoning trace and executable action under an empty memory channel.
evidence.support_explanation: OFF rollouts train the policy to act without the memory block.

evidence.quote: ATMem-UI (Ours) | 8B | 76.6
evidence.support_explanation: AndroidWorld SR for the 8B model.

evidence.quote: UI-TARS-2 ( Wang et al., 2025a ) | 230B | 73.3
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-paper reference value (UI-TARS-2 reports 73.3, E040).

evidence.quote: MAI-UI ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) | 8B | 70.7
evidence.support_explanation: Same-size baseline reference.

evidence.quote: ATMem-UI (Ours) | 8B | 23.3
evidence.support_explanation: MobileWorld SR for the 8B model.

evidence.quote: UI-Venus-1.5 ( Team et al., 2026 ) | 30B | 17.1
evidence.support_explanation: Strongest listed reference on MobileWorld; 23.3 vs 17.1 is the claimed 36.2% relative gain.

evidence.quote: where all environments are unseen during training
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' statement that MobileWorld is an unseen environment.
Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct base under the authors' protocol: AndroidWorld 47.6, MobileWorld 9.4.
After SFT on verifier-gated in-domain ATMem trajectories: +23.1 on AndroidWorld, +7.8 on MobileWorld.
Standard GRPO stage.
STR-GRPO: +1.8/+2.6 over GRPO and 13.8/14.6 points less memory use.

evidence.quote: AndroidWorld consists of a suite of 116 tasks, spread across 20 diverse applications
evidence.support_explanation: Denominator for AndroidWorld results: 116 tasks.

Over 116 tasks, 70.7 (=82/116) and 65.5 (=76/116) are single-run counts but 76.6, 74.8 and 47.6 are not (89/116=76.7, 87/116=75.0, 55/116=47.4); an unreported averaging or different task set is used for the authors' own numbers.
DataScope results: SR 6.2/6.2/3.1.
Strongest end-to-end baseline on DataScope.

evidence.quote: Each level contains 32 task instances, yielding 96 instances across 14 mobile apps.
evidence.support_explanation: 32 tasks per difficulty level.
SR values are multiples of 3.125 (2/32, 2/32, 1/32): ATMem-UI beats the best end-to-end baseline by one task at DC-V1, V2 and V3.
The teacher-class framework scores 18.8 SR at DC-V1, 12.6 above the student.

evidence.quote: DataScope directly probes the capabilities ATMem is designed to support
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark was designed by the same authors around the method's targeted capability.

evidence.quote: A verifier is retained only if its score matches the expected score for all controlled variants; otherwise, the task case is returned for manual correction.
evidence.support_explanation: DataScope verifiers are calibrated against controlled terminal states.

evidence.quote: GPT-5.2 generates multiple perturbed terminal states, including successful completion, missing one or more required data operations, extra operations on non-target data, missing operations in a particular app, and incorrect field values.
evidence.support_explanation: Calibration covers false positives on faulty states; alternative legal terminal states are not listed.

evidence.quote: Stuck loops are the dominant failure mode at 40.9%, followed by wrong termination (21.9%), step cap (21.4%), and miscellaneous errors, including grounding failures and environment edge cases (15.8%).
evidence.support_explanation: Failure breakdown given for MAI-UI-8B only.

evidence.quote: These failures are not fully solved by item-level status tracking alone.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors bound the scope: termination and step-cap failures remain.

evidence.quote: because task-level reward does not distinguish whether a successful trajectory succeeded due to ATMem or despite it
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' rationale for STR-GRPO.

evidence.quote: For online RL, we use the same 128-GPU training configuration and train for about 3 days.
evidence.support_explanation: Online RL compute (128 NVIDIA H20, ~3 days; SFT ~2 hours).

evidence.quote: and 73.3 on AndroidWorld
evidence.support_explanation: The 73.3 reference is UI-TARS-2's own reported number under its own protocol.

evidence.quote: To isolate the effect of memory structure, we run the same agentic framework on identical tasks, changing only the memory format.
evidence.support_explanation: The only controlled memory-format comparison is with a prompted GPT-5 planner framework and one worked example; numeric results are in a figure not present in the text.

evidence.quote: With the same GPT-5 planner and UIIns grounding framework, ATMem improves over flat-memory and full-history baselines
evidence.support_explanation: Bar-chart claim for the prompted framework (values not in text).

evidence.quote: While these works highlight the importance of memory for long-horizon GUI execution, they mainly represent memory as reusable experience, recorded notes, retrieved context, or program/interface state.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' delta statement over note-taking, anchored-state and program-state neighbors (not in the fixed set).

evidence.quote: Mem. denotes the fraction of tasks in which the agent invokes ATMem at least once during execution.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory-usage metric used to argue 'selective' use.

evidence.quote: AWM flexibly applies to both offline and online scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: AWM is cross-episode workflow memory; ATMem is within-episode state, so they address different memory roles.

evidence.quote: a skill-centric framework that enables agents to self-improve by autonomously synthesizing reusable skills as APIs
evidence.support_explanation: SkillWeaver: cross-episode skills; same distinction.
No repeated runs, seeds, intervals or run-to-run spread are reported for any success rate.
No fine-tuned control without the ATMem block (SFT or RL on the same verified trajectories with the memory field removed) is reported for the 8B model; Table 4 starts from the un-tuned base.
No decontamination or template-overlap analysis between the 120 training templates, the 20-app training platform, AndroidWorld tasks and DataScope templates appears anywhere.
The observation setting (screenshot-only versus accessibility tree) and the evaluation step budget for AndroidWorld/MobileWorld are not stated.
No per-step token, latency or inference-cost figure for generating and carrying the ATMem block is reported.
In MAI-UI's own MobileWorld table (columns GUI-Only (116), User-Int. (45), MCP (40), Overall) MAI-UI-8B scores 27.5 on GUI-Only, above ATMem-UI-8B's 23.3.
Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS scores 26.3 on MobileWorld GUI-Only, also above 23.3; ATMem lists it among its baselines yet omits it from Table 2.

Base Qwen3-VL-8B = 9.4 on MobileWorld GUI-Only (116): equals the ATMem baseline row, and UI-Venus-72B 16.4, GUI-Owl-7B 7.7, UI-Venus-7B 8.5 equal ATMem Table 2 entries, so Table 2 appears to be the GUI-Only (116) column with MAI-UI-8B and Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS removed.

evidence.quote: outperforming the strongest non-ours baseline, GELab-Zero-4B, by 7.2 points
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' claim about the strongest baseline on MobileWorld; contradicted by E052/E053.

evidence.quote: MAI-UI-32B, MAI-UI-8B, and MAI-UI-2B attain success rate of 73.3% , 70.7% , and 49.1% on AndroidWorld
evidence.support_explanation: MAI-UI's AndroidWorld numbers (8B: 70.7) equal ATMem Table 1; MAI-UI-235B reports 76.7, so 76.6 at 8B is the best listed but not above the largest MAI-UI.

signatures.object: Per-step memory block m_t carried in the system prompt of a screenshot policy
signatures.information: Policy sees instruction c, current GUI observation o_t, interaction history h_<t and its own previous ATMem block m_t; no privileged environment state.
signatures.operation: At every step emit (m_{t+1}, reasoning, action); m holds Phase (harvest/execute), RemainingFiles/CompletedFiles, Constraints, locked Schema fields and ItemContent entries with status remaining/finished/skipped; the model may leave m empty when not needed.
signatures.output: Updated structured state used in the next prompt.
signatures.conditions: Workflows where task progress depends on the status of data units across pages/apps; the model must write correct statuses.
signatures.feedback: Verifier outcome only at episode end; no check that status updates are correct.
signatures.selection_rule_data: SFT keeps teacher trajectories that pass the task verifier; STR-GRPO learns when to keep m non-empty.
signatures.later_use: Next step's prompt; checklist drives which item to process next.
signatures.claimed_effect: Fewer repeated/missed operations; AndroidWorld 47.6->76.6 for the full recipe (E022, E025).
signatures.failure_boundary: Wrong termination (21.9% of baseline failures) and step-cap exhaustion are not addressed by item status (E036, E037); status-update accuracy unmeasured.

signatures.information: GPT-5-class planner + UIIns grounding generate rollouts on 1.1K executable instances from 120 human-designed templates with initializers and verifiers; teacher is prompted to maintain ATMem when needed.
signatures.operation: Instantiate templates with an LLM generator, run teacher rollouts, keep only verifier-passing trajectories.
signatures.output: 21,713 step-level samples mapping (c, o_t, h_<t, m_t) -> (m_{t+1}, reasoning, action).
signatures.later_use: initialization for online RL and for evaluation
signatures.failure_boundary: Training platform has 20 apps like AndroidWorld; overlap with evaluation not analysed (E012, E049).

signatures.information: Balanced memory-ON/OFF cohorts per task group (16 rollouts), outcome reward from task verifier, memory-active fraction rho for ON rollouts.
signatures.operation: R = V(terminal) - alpha*z*rho; group-normalized advantage across the mixed cohort; OFF rollouts mask ATMem tokens from the loss.
signatures.selection_rule_data: ON/OFF assignment is balanced, not chosen
signatures.claimed_effect: +1.8/+2.6 SR and -13.8/-14.6 memory-usage points over standard GRPO (E024, E025).
signatures.failure_boundary: Single run; no no-ATMem RL control.

signatures.information: 32 hand-designed templates x 3 difficulty levels, with initializers writing targets and same-schema distractors; verifiers inspect terminal app state.
signatures.operation: Scale targets and distractors (ratio 1.39x -> 3.22x) while holding operation schema fixed; add App-Progress and Scope-F1; calibrate verifiers on controlled terminal states.
signatures.failure_boundary: Tiny per-level n (32); same group as method (E033).

retention_trace.reason: system_method claim without cross-task retention: ATMem lives within one episode and is not accumulated across tasks. The training chain is recorded as a static pipeline.

chain.proposed_change: SFT on 21,713 verified ATMem steps, then STR-GRPO (E009, E013-E015)
chain.selection_data_rule: verifier-gated teacher trajectories; balanced ON/OFF cohorts with cost term

gap.author_gap: Passive record memory (history, summaries, notes, retrieval) preserves what was seen but not each value's role/status, causing repeated or missed operations in long, data-dependent workflows (E003, E004).
gap.checked_gap: A concrete and plausible failure mode is documented: stuck loops are 40.9% of the strongest end-to-end baseline's DataScope failures (E036) and a worked flat-notes example loops until the 100-step cap. The delta is argued against notes/anchored-state/program-state neighbors (E043) that are outside the fixed set; AWM and SkillWeaver (E045, E046) are cross-episode and address a different memory role. The decisive comparison for the trained 8B model (same data, memory field removed) is absent.

lineage_closest_adjacent.source: Mobile-Agent-v2/E-style notes and focus-content memory (named by paper; not in fixed set)
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: no per-item status or constraints (author claim)

gap.residue: Whether structured status tracking itself (versus in-domain verified SFT + RL) produces the gain; whether status updates are accurate; termination and step-cap failures.
gap.stakes: Long cross-app data workflows (83% of AndroidWorld tasks involve data operations by the authors' count).
gap.method_response: Make the state explicit, schema-locked and item-status-bearing; calibrate its use by interventional RL.
gap.remaining_gap: Wrong termination, step caps, state-update correctness, no-ATMem fine-tuned control, repeated runs.
gap.unresolved: Attribution of the 47.6 -> 76.6 gain between ATMem structure and in-domain verified data/RL.

rs_pattern.reason: Central operations are (i) an agent-maintained structured execution-state block carried in the prompt and (ii) interventional memory-on/off online RL with a usage-cost term. Candidates read in full: structural_prior_encoding (card definition requires the structure to hold by construction; ATMem is a learned, unguaranteed prompt format, and sub-cards C13/C16/C20 target relational topology, symmetry groups and corruption processes), decompose_and_delegate/C25 (needs an external sound solver closing the loop; none exists here), self_supervised_signal_engineering/C26 (rewards come from an executable verifier, not a manufactured signal), assumption_audit_and_pivot (sub-cards concern theory/security assumptions). The benchmark half resembles controlled_diagnostic_design/C02 (matched templates, scaling distractors, calibrated verifiers) but it is a secondary contribution, so it is not scored as a supporting match. No forced label is assigned.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: repeated/missed-operation failures are argued and the full recipe improves online success, but ATMem structure is not isolated for the trained model

claims.text: ATMem-UI-8B reaches 76.6% on AndroidWorld, beating UI-TARS-2-230B (73.3) and the same-size MAI-UI (70.7).
claims.baseline_control: published numbers from other papers (E017, E018, E040)
claims.selection_vs_test: training platform has 20 apps like AndroidWorld; overlap unanalysed
claims.result_denominator: not a k/116 count (E027); step cap and observation setting unstated
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under the authors' unspecified protocol the model scores above listed published numbers; the comparison is cross-paper.

claims.text: ATMem generalizes to unseen environments: MobileWorld 23.3% (8B), 36.2% relative over the strongest baseline.
claims.baseline_control: own base 9.4 (equals the independently published Qwen3-VL-8B 9.4); listed references 16.1-17.1
claims.result_denominator: single run; the published column also contains MAI-UI-8B 27.5 and Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS 26.3 that ATMem's table omits

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: The full recipe (SFT on 21,713 verifier-gated ATMem steps then STR-GRPO) takes Qwen3-VL-8B from 47.6 to 76.6 on AndroidWorld and from 9.4 to 23.3 on MobileWorld, an environment stated as unseen, in the authors' single-run protocol; STR-GRPO cuts memory-active use by about 14 points at equal or higher SR than standard GRPO. assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; nothing was re-run.
assessment.evidence_level_note: 'transfer' rests on MobileWorld (authors state all its environments are unseen) with a same-protocol base comparison; AndroidWorld alone would be 'online' because the training platform has the same app count and its construction practice.

G.reason: A concrete, documented failure mode (repeated, missed and over-scoped operations; stuck loops 40.9% of the strongest baseline's DataScope failures) is tied to a specific representational gap, and residual failures are scoped by the authors; neighbors are partly named but the note-taking/anchored-state/program-state neighbors are outside the fixed set and not compared head-to-head.

M.reason: Explicit schema-locked item-status state plus ON/OFF-interventional RL is a coherent answer to the stated gap and yields distinguishable predictions (fewer stuck loops, higher scope-F1, lower memory use at equal SR), partly supported; the key assumption that the model writes correct statuses is untested, and the trained-model attribution control is missing.

X.reason: State fields, statuses, SFT pipeline (templates, initializers, verifiers, filtering), RL objective, cohorts, hyper-parameters and infrastructure are specified, and remaining failure classes are bounded; prompts and listings are absent from the text render, update-correctness checks do not exist, and the evaluation protocol (steps, observation) is unstated.

E.measurement.reason: Execution-based verifiers on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld plus DataScope verifiers calibrated on controlled perturbed terminal states are good; but the MobileWorld comparison table omits stronger published end-to-end results from the same column (MAI-UI-8B 27.5, Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS 26.3) so the competitive claim is contradicted, baselines are cross-paper under unknown protocols, and own numbers are not k/116 counts.

E.causality.reason: Stage ablation (base, SFT, GRPO, STR-GRPO) and a GPT-5-framework memory-format comparison give partial attribution, but no fine-tuned control without the ATMem block, the +23 SFT gain is on in-domain verified data, and baselines in the tables lack equal in-domain training.

E.holdout.reason: MobileWorld is stated unseen and shows a same-protocol base-to-final gain, but the 20-app training platform and template-based tasks parallel AndroidWorld, no overlap analysis is given, and DataScope is by the same authors around the method's target capability.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs; DataScope SR differences are one task out of 32 per level; STR-GRPO margins are 2-3 tasks; own AndroidWorld values are non-integer counts without explanation.

E.cost.reason: Training compute (128 H20 GPUs, SFT 2 h, RL 3 days) and memory-usage fraction are reported, but evaluation step budgets, per-step token/latency overhead of the memory block and comparable compute for baselines are not.

status.reason: Full html text read including appendix A; figures, prompt boxes and the template listing are images or code boxes absent from the text render, which affects only Figure 1(d) numbers and exact prompts.

rationale.summary: ATMem makes the agent write and update a structured execution state (phase, constraints, locked schema, per-item remaining/finished/skipped) every step, trained with SFT on verifier-passing teacher rollouts and a memory-on/off interventional GRPO that charges for unnecessary memory use. The full recipe lifts Qwen3-VL-8B from 47.6 to 76.6 on AndroidWorld and from 9.4 to 23.3 on MobileWorld, and the DataScope benchmark shows that scope tracking is hard for all agents. The problem diagnosis is concrete, and the verifier calibration is better than typical, but ATMem's contribution is not separated from in-domain data and RL for the trained model, results are single-run, and DataScope differences are one task per level.
strengths: Concrete failure-mode diagnosis and bounded residual failures
Interventional ON/OFF design with a measured memory-usage metric
Verifier calibration with controlled perturbed terminal states
MobileWorld unseen-environment result with an own-protocol base
weaknesses: MobileWorld table omits MAI-UI-8B (27.5) and Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS (26.3), both above 23.3, so 'strongest on MobileWorld' is contradicted
No fine-tuned control without the ATMem block; gain mostly from in-domain verified SFT
Single runs; non-integer own AndroidWorld counts; SR margins of 1-3 tasks
Cross-paper baselines; evaluation protocol (steps, observation) unstated
